fixup! Bug 2061218 - Save calendar event edits in new calendar edit dialog. r=#thunderbird-front-end-reviewers

Failure causes:
test_onlySaveButtonInvokesSave still constructed MouseEvent("click") for privileged fixture targets. The related repair links this expression to debug-process crashes in jobs 600289473, 600289502, 600289509, 600289530, 600289560, 600289569, and 600289621. Current Gecko source retains the constructor assertion: "Please use PointerEvent constructor!" Current source inspection confirms that the expression remained after the previous fixup.

The supplied classifications remain unchanged for all ten latest jobs: 601688854, 601688843, 601688849, 601688841, 601688851, 601688844, 601688855, 601688853, 601688848, and 601688845. They report existing vendored-Rust synchronization failures and Glean locked at 70.3.0 with only 70.2.1 available. These classifications were not independently revalidated. No unknown classification was resolved.

Changes:
Changed only mail/components/calendar/test/browser/browser_calendarEventEditSave.js: four added lines and five removed lines. The two non-Save routing checks now query each real target, assert that the target exists, and call dialog.handleEvent({ type: "click", target }). A short comment explains why the empty body uses a direct routing check. This removes the crashing constructor while retaining the production routing logic and all existing assertions.

Reused the exact routing block from related repair f8159051d252bf446130760cd10da256108e59ce. Preserved both enabled-Save mouse activations, keyboard navigation, accessibility checks, draft checks, and storage checks. The target-existence assertion has an expected-behavior message containing should and runs for both targets.

Compared the sourceUpdates revisions and prior fixup cd6b31864a5389490d26b06f5830262ef232fbba with current source. The More-button keyboard sequence, disabled-Save click(), opener assertion message, detached-render guard, and lifecycle regression test are already present. Those repairs were preserved without duplication. The actual diff follows the prepared evidence record without departures. No production files or shared rules changed.

Validation:
Passed node --check for browser_calendarEventEditSave.js and git diff --check. Passed ESLint 9.39.1 with caching disabled and zero errors or warnings, using this checkout's configuration and current in-tree Mozilla and SDL plugins. Passed Prettier 3.8.5 with the file's resolved configuration.

An AST source audit confirmed that all 136 existing assertion calls remain exactly unchanged. The repair adds one assertion call. All seven assertion sites in the repaired task have non-empty expected-behavior messages containing should. Both enabled-Save pointer activations remain. A separate comparison confirmed that the changed routing block exactly matches the existing related repair. Its completed native routing experiment was reused as reported evidence and was not repeated.

Attempted the official Mochitest harness for browser_calendarEventEditSave.js with AUTOCLOBBER=1, MOZ_HEADLESS=1, --flavor browser, --subsuite thunderbird, --headless, and --enable-a11y-checks. Copied the harness and current Calendar tests into comm/obj-repair-validation. The command exited 1 before launching Thunderbird because psutil.process_iter() raised PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted (originated from sysctl() malloc 1/3). The log is obj-repair-validation/browser.log.

Final scope checks passed. Only the intended test file is modified. Nothing is staged, and HEAD remains 36c4c4e8284c901ba4b7d3adab9ad462ed0b6175.

Validation limits:
No native browser or accessibility test completed. The available build reports SourceStamp=unknown, so matching-source runtime validation remains unproven. No build, full Try, or regression failure-sensitivity run completed. The commlint wrapper was not repeated after its documented setup-write failures; direct ESLint and Prettier checks completed separately.

The evidence assessment remains incomplete. The accepted local routing example supports target lookup, existence assertions, and direct control calls, but no accepted Calendar browser-test example demonstrates this exact handleEvent call. This repair is a scoped implementation choice supported by current source and the related repair; it does not establish shared guidance. The related report's visible-selector-label concern remains unresolved by browser execution.

All diagnostic writes stayed inside this comm checkout. No visible browser, accessibility-check suppression, commits, staging, Git ref changes, or shared-rule changes were used.

--- a/mail/components/calendar/test/browser/browser_calendarEventEditSave.js
+++ b/mail/components/calendar/test/browser/browser_calendarEventEditSave.js
@@ -223,15 +223,14 @@ add_task(async function test_onlySaveButtonInvokesSave() {
   await edit(original);
   dialog.updateDraftSection("title", { title: "After Save" });
 
+  // The empty body has no pointer target. Check its Save routing directly.
   for (const selector of [
     ".calendar-selector",
     ".calendar-event-create-edit-dialog-body",
   ]) {
-    dialog
-      .querySelector(selector)
-      .dispatchEvent(
-        new browser.contentWindow.MouseEvent("click", { bubbles: true })
-      );
+    const target = dialog.querySelector(selector);
+    Assert.ok(target, `${selector} should exist in the dialog.`);
+    dialog.handleEvent({ type: "click", target });
 
     Assert.equal(calls, 0, `${selector} clicks should not invoke Save.`);
   }
